Privacy notice

What personal data Week2Speak collects, why, who else handles it, how long we keep it, and the rights you have.

Last updated 11 November 2026

Who we are

Week2Speak is run by Mei Gabriela Parrablanco, a sole trader based in the United Kingdom. Mei Gabriela Parrablanco is the data controller for the personal data described here. Contact us about anything in this notice at hello@week2speak.com.

The short version

  • Practising on this website does not send your answers to us. Your progress is saved only in your own browser.
  • We only collect your name and contact details if you ask for a place, and we use them only to arrange it.
  • We record lessons only with your permission, and we ask separately before using any clip publicly. You can say no to both and still take part.
  • We do not sell your data, use advertising cookies, or track you across other websites.

Recordings and clips

Before your first lesson we ask two separate questions, and neither box is ticked for you:

  1. May we record your lessons so you and your tutor can hear your progress?
  2. May we use short clips of you on our website or social media?

You can agree to the first and not the second, or to neither. You can change your mind at any time by messaging your tutor or emailing hello@week2speak.com. If you withdraw permission for public clips, we stop using them and remove the ones we control. We say "I'm recording now" at the start of every recorded part of a lesson.

Cookies and browser storage

This website does not set cookies and does not use analytics or advertising trackers. It saves your practice progress in your browser's local storage so it is still there when you come back. Recordings you make on the Sprint page are kept in the same way. That data stays on your device. You can delete it with the "Clear practice data on this device" button on the Tutor view page, or by clearing site data in your browser settings.

Where they do, they rely on legal safeguards such as standard contractual clauses or the UK-US data bridge. We store learner recordings on our own computer, not with a transcription service.

How long we keep it

  • Join requests from people who do not go on to join: 12 months, then deleted.
  • Lesson notes, voice notes and recordings: while you are a learner, then 12 months after your last lesson, then deleted.
  • Clips you agreed to publish: until you withdraw permission.
  • Payment and tax records: as long as UK tax law requires, currently at least 5 years after the relevant tax return deadline.

Your rights

Under UK and EU data protection law (UK GDPR and the GDPR) you can ask us to:

  • give you a copy of the personal data we hold about you;
  • correct data that is wrong or incomplete;
  • delete your data;
  • restrict or object to how we use it;
  • give you your data in a format you can take elsewhere;
  • withdraw any consent you gave, at any time, without affecting what we did before.

Learners in Mexico have the equivalent rights of access, rectification, cancellation and opposition under Mexico's Federal Law on the Protection of Personal Data Held by Private Parties. Learners in Colombia can know, update and correct their data and revoke their authorisation under Law 1581 of 2012.

To use any of these rights, email hello@week2speak.com. We reply within one month. It is free.

Complaints

If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, please contact us first so we can put it right. You can also complain to a data protection authority:

  • United Kingdom: the Information Commissioner's Office, ico.org.uk
  • Spain: the Agencia Española de Protección de Datos, aepd.es
  • Colombia: the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio, sic.gov.co
  • Mexico: the federal authority responsible for personal data protection

Age

Week2Speak is for adults aged 18 and over. We do not knowingly collect data from anyone younger.

Changes to this notice

If we change how we use your data, we update this page and the date at the top. If a change affects you as a learner, we tell you directly before it applies.
